title: The point transport along Frobenius is linear and natural
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ contained in $\Qlb$, $n\geq1$, $s=\Spec k$ and $g_s=\Spec(\operatorname{Frob}_q):s\to s$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Let $\sigma_N$ and $\iota_N$ be the maps of the point transport [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport], $\kappa_N$ and $c_\Lambda$ the comparison morphism and structure isomorphism of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison] for $g=g_s$, $Lg_s^*$ the derived pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ the point fiber functor [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Then:

1. For $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E\}$ and every complex $N$ of $\Lambda_s$-modules on $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], $\sigma_N:\Gamma(s,N)\to\Gamma(s,g_s^{-1}N)$ is $\Lambda$-linear, $\Lambda$ acting on $\Gamma(s,N)$ through $\Lambda\to\Gamma(s,\Lambda_s)$ and on $\Gamma(s,g_s^{-1}N)$ through $\Lambda\to\Gamma(s,\Lambda_s)$ and $c_\Lambda^{-1}$; $\sigma_N$ is natural in morphisms of complexes $N\to N'$; hence, $\Gamma(s,-)$ [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] and $g_s^{-1}$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] being exact, the $\sigma_N$ define a natural transformation $\Gamma(s,-)\to\Gamma(s,g_s^{-1}(-))$ of functors $D(s_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)\to D(\Lambda)$.

2. For each $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$ the morphisms $\iota_N$, $N\in D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], form a natural transformation $\iota:\operatorname{Fib}_s\to\operatorname{Fib}_s\circ Lg_s^*$ of functors on $D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$: for every morphism $u:N\to N'$ of $D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$, $\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lg_s^*u)\circ\iota_N=\iota_{N'}\circ\operatorname{Fib}_s(u)$. For $\Lambda=\Qlb$ this includes the compatibility of $\iota^{E'}$ with the scalar extensions $E'\subset L$, under the isomorphisms $\operatorname{Fib}_s(K\otimes_{E'}L)\cong\operatorname{Fib}_s(K)\otimes_{E'}L$ of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] and $(Lg_{s,E'}^*K)\otimes_{E'}L\cong Lg_{s,L}^*(K\otimes_{E'}L)$ of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension].

source.place: Deligne, La conjecture de Weil II, (1.1.7), pp. 150-151 (the action of Gal(k-bar/k) on the fibre by transport of structure, used as functorial); the statement for the explicit point transport of def-weil-frobenius-point-transport is written by an agent (split off from that definition, which asserted it without proof)

proof.text: Write $g=g_s$, $U=(s\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}s)$ and $V=(s\xrightarrow g s)$. The evaluation isomorphism $(g^{-1}M)(U)\simeq M(V)$ in [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image](1) identifies the specified coprojection/sheafification in [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] with evaluation at $V$: at the distinguished index the map $U\to u_g(V)$ is the indicated diagonal, and reindexing along the inverse site equivalence sends it to $\mathrm{id}_V$. More explicitly, $(V,\mathrm{diagonal})$ is initial in the indexing category $\mathcal I_U$: a map $U\to u_g(W)$ is uniquely a map $V\to W$ under this equivalence. It is therefore terminal in $\mathcal I_U^{\mathrm{op}}$, so the colimit is $M(V)$ with that coprojection the identity. These identifications are natural in $U$, hence already a sheaf, and sheafification preserves them. Thus $\sigma_M$ is restriction along $g:V\to U$ under this identification. Restriction respects addition and the module action. For a finite coefficient $a$, the structure map of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] sends the pulled-back constant section $a$ to the constant section $a$; hence $\sigma_{\Lambda_s}(a)=c_\Lambda^{-1}(a)$. For integral $a\in\mathcal O_E$ the same equality follows after every projection to $A_{E,m}$, using the defining formula for $c_{\mathcal O_E}$ in [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]; equality in the ordinary sheaf inverse limit is equality of all coordinates. Consequently $\sigma_M(ax)=c_\Lambda^{-1}(a)\sigma_M(x)$, which is precisely linearity for the action in clause (1), also for the completed coefficient sheaf.

proof.text: For a chain map $u:N\to N'$, sheaf-map naturality says $u(V)\operatorname{res}_g=\operatorname{res}_g u(U)$; the functorial colimit coprojection and sheafification in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] say $(g^{-1}u)(U)\operatorname{ins}_N=\operatorname{ins}_{N'}u(V)$. Composition gives $\Gamma(s,g^{-1}u)\sigma_N=\sigma_{N'}\Gamma(s,u)$. Apply this also to each differential; the maps are linear maps of complexes. Sections preserve quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact], and the module inverse-image functor does so by [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. The localization defining $D$ in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] is generated by chain maps and formal inverses of quasi-isomorphisms. For an inverted map $v$, its naturality equation gives the equation for $v^{-1}$ by multiplying by the two inverses. It therefore gives the equation for every finite composite of generators. This descends $\sigma$ and its naturality to the asserted derived functors, without a boundedness or completeness hypothesis on $N$.

source.place: (1.1.3), p. 150 (rationalization and finite coefficient fields), and (1.1.7), pp. 150-151 (transport of structure). Explicit complex-level argument written by an agent.

proof.text: At finite level the comparison in [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison](a) is $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. For a chain map $u$, both paths in its naturality square send $x$ to $g^{-1}u(x)\otimes1$, and sheafification preserves this equality. The same formal-inverse calculation of Step 2 gives $Lg_s^*(u)\kappa_N=\kappa_{N'}g_s^{-1}(u)$ for every derived morphism. This proves naturality of the specified finite comparison, rather than choosing some isomorphism between the functors.

source.place: (1.1.3), p. 150 (rationalization and finite coefficient fields), and (1.1.7), pp. 150-151 (transport of structure). Explicit complex-level argument written by an agent.

proof.text:
At integral level use [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback-comparison-normalization], applicable because $g_s$ is an isomorphism and $\ell$ is invertible on $s$. It identifies the SPECIFIED $\kappa_N$ with $\theta_{g,N}^{-1}G(u_N)$, where $G=g_s^{-1}$, $u$ is the actual natural completion unit, and $\theta$ is natural for derived morphisms. Thus for $v:N\to N'$,
$$Lg_s^*(v)\kappa_N=\theta_{g,N'}^{-1}G(\widehat v)G(u_N)=\theta_{g,N'}^{-1}G(u_{N'})G(v)=\kappa_{N'}G(v).$$
This uses the whole strict-cone normalization in the cited statement; equality of maps to individual reductions would not suffice.

source.place: (1.1.3), p. 150 (rationalization and finite coefficient fields), and (1.1.7), pp. 150-151 (transport of structure). Explicit complex-level argument written by an agent.

proof.text:
For $\Lambda=A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E$, [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback] ensures that $Lg_s^*$ preserves the indicated constructible category. The point functor is sections there by [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], and [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] defines $\iota_N=\Gamma(s,\kappa_N)\sigma_N$. Composing the squares in Steps 2-4 yields
$$\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lg_s^*v)\iota_N=\Gamma(s,\kappa_{N'})\Gamma(s,g_s^{-1}v)\sigma_N=\iota_{N'}\operatorname{Fib}_s(v).$$
These are maps in the full bounded point categories, so the same equality proves the required natural transformation there.

proof.text: For $\Lambda=E$, [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] gives the same integral objects and morphisms that are finite sums $\sum_j v_j\otimes a_j$. By [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], the fiber sends this to $\sum_j a_j(\Gamma(s,v_j)\otimes E)$, and [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] gives $\iota^E_N=\iota^{\mathcal O_E}_N\otimes E$. The rational pullback is the scalar-localized integral operation [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Tensor the integral naturality equality with $E$, multiply by $a_j$, and add over $j$. This gives naturality for every rational morphism; it includes morphisms not represented by a single integral chain map.

source.place: (1.1.3), p. 150 (rationalization and finite coefficient fields), and (1.1.7), pp. 150-151 (transport of structure). Explicit complex-level argument written by an agent.

proof.text:
Fix a finite extension $E\subset L$ and put $T=-\widehat\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$. Let $\beta_K:T(g_s^{-1}K)\simeq g_s^{-1}(TK)$ be the explicitly defined isomorphism in [lem-weil-isomorphism-comparison-scalar-extension]. The sections comparison $\varphi_H:\Gamma(s,TH)\simeq\Gamma(s,H)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$ is the inverse of sections-tensor followed by $\Gamma(s,\chi_H)$ by [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]. Define $\psi_K=(\varphi_{g_s^{-1}K})\circ\Gamma(s,\beta_K)^{-1}$. Then
$$\psi_K\sigma_{TK}=(\sigma_K\otimes1)\varphi_K.$$
To check this, use the specified $\chi$ to replace $T$ by ordinary finite free tensor [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. On a local pure tensor $x\otimes b$, restriction and the distinguished inverse-image coprojection send it to $\operatorname{ins}(x|_V)\otimes b$ in either order: restriction fixes the constant coefficient $b$, and the tensor comparison sends the inverse image of a pure tensor to the tensor of the inverse images. This is exactly the local formula for $b_K$ and hence for $\beta_K$. Additivity and the tensor relations give equality of the sheaf maps. Step 2 applied to the derived map $\chi_K$ moves $\sigma$ through $\chi_K$. The two $\chi$ factors then cancel by the displayed definition of $\beta$; the defining formula for $\varphi$ then gives the written equation on derived sections. The objects to which $\varphi$ is applied are constructible by [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback].

source.place: (1.1.3), p. 150 (rationalization and finite coefficient fields), and (1.1.7), pp. 150-151 (transport of structure). Explicit complex-level argument written by an agent.

proof.text:
Let $\alpha_K:T(Lg_{s,E}^*K)\simeq Lg_{s,L}^*(TK)$ be the canonical comparison of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]. By [lem-weil-isomorphism-comparison-scalar-extension], $\alpha_K T(\kappa^{E}_K)=\kappa^{L}_{TK}\beta_K$. Naturality of $\varphi$ in [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] and Step 7 therefore give
$$\varphi_{Lg_{s,E}^*K}\Gamma(s,\alpha_K)^{-1}\iota^{\mathcal O_L}_{TK}=(\iota^{\mathcal O_E}_K\otimes1)\varphi_K.$$
Indeed substitute $\iota=\Gamma(\kappa)\sigma$, replace $\Gamma(\alpha)^{-1}\Gamma(\kappa^L)$ by $\Gamma(T\kappa^E)\Gamma(\beta)^{-1}$, move $\Gamma(T\kappa^E)$ through $\varphi$ using its naturality, and apply Step 7. Tensor with $L$ to get precisely compatibility of $\iota^E$ with rational coefficient extension, under the displayed sections/scalar-extension and pullback/scalar-extension comparisons. Their identity and successive-extension coherences are those in the two cited scalar-extension lemmas. Thus this equality persists after any further finite coefficient extension.

source.place: (1.1.3), p. 150 (rationalization and finite coefficient fields), and (1.1.7), pp. 150-151 (transport of structure). Explicit complex-level argument written by an agent.

proof.text: Finally a morphism between $(E,K)$ and $(E',K')$ in [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] is represented over some common finite field $L$ by $v:K\otimes_EL\to K'\otimes_{E'}L$. The fiber functor acts on it by conjugating $\operatorname{Fib}_s(v)$ with the scalar comparisons [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. The pullback acts on it by conjugating $Lg_{s,L}^*(v)$ with the rationalized pullback/scalar-extension comparisons $\alpha$ of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], as specified at the algebraically closed level of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. By Step 8 the scalar extension of each point-transport component equals the component at that common stage. Hence the desired naturality square is, after those conjugations, exactly the $L$-naturality square proved in Step 6. It commutes. A further extension preserves this equality by Step 8, and equality in the morphism colimit is equality at a further common stage. Consequently the result is independent of the representative and proves clause (2) for $\Qlb$.
